answer: Deposits are visible in crystal, and hollow reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 35% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 130 aliases, and each one needs its own funded falcon account. That bill is paid per identity, so 217 aliases cost 87 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
